newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Guangdong Tannery ends debut sharply up.
newsitem.headline: Guangdong Tannery ends debut sharply up.

text.p: Shares of Guangdong Tannery Ltd, a leather spinoff of Guangdong Investment Ltd, ended their trading debut at HK$2.05 per share on Monday, almost double the issue price of HK$1.03.
The shares moved in a range of HK$2.05 to HK$2.60 on volume of 72.32 million shares worth HK$165.59 million.
Analysts said the price surged on high demand for the stock following its high subscription rate.
"They are not buying on fundamentals. They are attracted to the stock because it was over 600 times subscribed," said an analyst who declined to be named.
He said people were buying the stock because they were expecting the company to receive an asset injection.

Guangdong Tannery offered a total of 110 million shares in Hong Kong. The 30 million shares offered for public subscription were 667 times subscribed, the highest subscription level for a Hong Kong initial public offering this year.
"However, I don't think this company will receive any asset injection in the short and medium term," said the analyst. "Also, being a tannery business, its potential for asset injection is limited."
Analysts said it will not be easy for the company to receive an injection of fresh assets as it would be beyond its core business and may not be approved by the stock exchange.
"Its parent company, Guangdong Investment, is more likely to receive a new asset injection as it is stronger and more flexible," the analyst said.
Analysts said the stock was considered to be fully valued at above the HK$2 level.
Dharmala Securities director of research Ben Kwong said the overall Tannery operation was professional and efficiently run.
"As there are not too many quality tannery manufacturers in China, its prospects are quite good," Kwong said.
Kwong said he expects the share price to trade higher as major players move in to pick up the stock after initial interest from retail investors.
Guangdong Tannery processes cow hides and sheep skins to make semi-finished and finished leather products.
The company said the net proceeds of the issue would be used to expand and upgrade production facilities in China.
